- [RCTS.1.2.26] **`introspection_assert`'s fields** — a fixture whose
  `expect.kind` is `introspection_assert` carries `steps`, the session's
  inputs as [RCTS.1.2.28] has them, and `checks`, a non-empty array of checks.
  A harness must run the steps, then read each check through the runtime's
  introspection surface ([LCON.4.5.1]). The runtime passes only when every
  check holds.

  A check is an object whose `surface` names one member of a closed set, and
  which carries exactly the members that surface takes:

  - `fact_count`, with `equals`, a non-negative integer: working memory holds
    that many live facts.
  - `justifiers`, with `fact_id`, a positive integer, and `expect_rules`, an
    array of rule names: the rules justifying that fact, by name and counted
    with repeats, are the array's.
  - `justifier_count`, with `fact_id` and `count`, a non-negative integer:
    that fact has that many justifications.
  - `rete_network`, with `min_nodes` and `min_edges`, non-negative integers:
    the network has at least that many nodes and at least that many edges.
  - `slot_schema_ref`, with `schema` and `slot`, strings, and `equals`, a
    string or `null`: the loaded schema `schema`'s slot `slot` names the
    schema `equals` as its reference, or none when `equals` is `null`
    ([RDSC.5.5.5]). The check fails when no such slot is loaded.
  - `slot_conversion`, with `schema` and `slot`, strings, `direction`, the
    string `to_stored` or `from_stored`, `in`, a number, and `equals`, a
    number or `null`: the loaded schema `schema`'s slot `slot` names a unit,
    and its conversion in that direction ([RDSC.5.5.9]), evaluated on `in` as
    a host's call evaluates it ([NFCT.1.4.6]), gives `equals`, of the same
    kind and with the same bits. When `equals` is `null`, the conversion
    raises a fault other than an `EngineError`, or gives a NaN, so it has no
    result for `in`. A number written with neither a fraction nor an exponent
    is an `Int`, and any other is a `Float`. The check fails when no such slot
    is loaded, when the slot names no unit, when `in` is not of the kind
    [NFCT.2.3] pairs with the slot's type, and when the conversion raises an
    `EngineError`.

  A `fact_id` names a fact by the id the runtime gave it ([RFCS.6.9]).

  `add_schema_ref` (optional, `introspection_assert` only) is an object of
  exactly three strings, `schema`, `slot` and `ref`. Before the load, a
  harness must give the compiled artefact's one `Slot` atom for `schema`'s
  slot `slot` a `schema_ref` of `ref`, written in ascending field order
  ([RFCS.19.5]), re-frame the atom, and recompute `dsc_sha256` as [RDSC.3.6]
  states. No compiler writes a `schema_ref` on a slot that is not a schema
  slot ([RDSC.5.5.5]), so this is how a fixture gives a runtime one to ignore.
  A harness must fail a fixture whose artefact holds no such `Slot`, more than
  one, or one that already carries a `schema_ref`.

  A harness must fail a fixture whose `checks` is not a non-empty array of
  objects; a check whose `surface` names no member of the set, or that lacks
  a member its surface takes, carries one it does not take, or gives one a
  value of another type; and an `add_schema_ref` of another shape. It must
  fail a fixture of any other `expect.kind` that carries `add_schema_ref`. The
  set grows only by a change to this clause.
